title: Metabolic organization of macaque visual cortex reflects visual field topography and perceptual specialization
experiments_summary: The study combined in vivo fMRI and ex vivo cytochrome oxidase (CO) histology from two macaque monkeys (M1 and M2) to examine metabolic architecture across visual cortex. Histological processing involved transcardial perfusion, sagittal sectioning of the right hemisphere at 50-µm thickness, and standard CO staining using cytochrome c, catalase, and DAB reagents. Digital images were normalized, white-matter-referenced for within-section intensity correction, and segmented into 15 equivolume cortical depth bins and columnar bins perpendicular to the cortical surface using LayNii. A 3D histological volume was reconstructed from serial sections via rigid-body and tissue-contrast-based co-registration in MATLAB. Functional ROIs (face-selective patch ML and scene-selective patch LPP) were defined using probabilistic fMRI group atlases (n=6 for face patches, n=9 for place patches, n=6 for retinotopy) constructed in NMT brain space, thresholded at 70% inter-subject consistency, and registered to the histological volume via nonlinear registration using the JIP Analysis Toolkit. Depth-resolved CO profiles within ML and LPP were compared using two-tailed unpaired t-tests across full depth, superficial (bins 1–7), and deep (bins 8–15) segments with FDR correction. To test CO-eccentricity relationships within ML and LPP, columnar bins were treated as individual data points; CO intensity and eccentricity values were z-scored per monkey, pooled, and correlated using Pearson's r, both across full depth and within superficial and deep segments. The same correlation approach was applied across all occipitotemporal cortical columnar bins overlapping with the projected eccentricity map. Probabilistic retinotopic area boundaries (V1 through PITd/v) were projected onto histological sections to assess mean CO and eccentricity per visual area across the ventral hierarchy. Group-average spatial frequency (SF) preference maps from four macaques were projected onto the histological volume and used in Pearson correlations and multiple regression models (with SF and eccentricity as co-predictors of CO, with partial R² and VIF computed) to control for SF as an alternative explanation. To assess whether CO differences between ML and LPP exceeded eccentricity-matched expectations, standardized residuals from a robust bisquare-weighted linear regression of CO on eccentricity were computed per columnar bin; an eccentricity-matched null distribution (5,000 iterations, matched eccentricity binned at 0.5° intervals) was constructed per ROI and evaluated using adjusted effect size, variance explained, and distributional overlap. Finally, to control for staining variability due to tissue size differences across sections, CO intensity was regressed against tissue size across all columnar bins, and residuals were used to confirm that CO-function relationships were not artifactual.
